A back-to-top link is a solved problem, and a dull one.
[Elevator.js](https://github.com/tholman/elevator.js) solves it differently: the page rides back up at a leisurely pace while elevator music plays, and dings when it arrives.

`elevator` wires that into Quarto as a shortcode.
One line gives you the button, the script, and the bundled arrival sound.

## Installation

```bash
quarto add {{< var extension.reference >}}
```

This will install the extension under the `_extensions` subdirectory.
If you are using version control, you will want to check in this directory.

Or install it from your editor with [Quarto Wizard](https://m.canouil.dev/quarto-wizard):

::: {.btn-group role="group" aria-label="Quarto Wizard installer options"}

[Visual Studio Code](vscode://mcanouil.quarto-wizard/install?repo={{< var extension.wizard-reference >}}){.btn .btn-outline-primary title="Install {{< var extension.reference >}} in Visual Studio Code using the Quarto Wizard extension."}
[Positron](positron://mcanouil.quarto-wizard/install?repo={{< var extension.wizard-reference >}}){.btn .btn-outline-primary title="Install {{< var extension.reference >}} in Positron using the Quarto Wizard extension."}
[VSCodium](vscodium://mcanouil.quarto-wizard/install?repo={{< var extension.wizard-reference >}}){.btn .btn-outline-primary title="Install {{< var extension.reference >}} in VSCodium using the Quarto Wizard extension."}

:::

## Quick start

```markdown
{{{< elevator >}}}
```

That is the whole thing: a button labelled "Return to the top!" that rides the page up and dings on arrival.

Give it your own label, and a target to stop at:

```markdown
{{{< elevator "Back to the header" my-header >}}}
```

Add the music, which is the point:

```markdown
{{{< elevator audio=music.mp3 volume=0.4 >}}}
```

See the [Reference](reference.qmd) for every option, and the [Examples](examples.qmd) for a button you can ride.

## Where it works

HTML formats that carry JavaScript, which covers `html` and `revealjs`.

::: {.callout-note}
In every other format the shortcode renders nothing, which is the right outcome: a scroll button means nothing in a PDF.
:::
